title: Trump Signs Executive Order on Beef Country-of-Origin Labeling
detail: President Trump signed an executive order behind closed doors at the White House on Friday, September 4, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. ET addressing country-of-origin labeling requirements for beef, sources familiar with the matter said. The move follows Trump's efforts to lower record-high beef prices, including an order last month temporarily allowing up to 300,000 metric tons of lower-tariff beef imports to enter the country without the higher 'out-of-quota' rate, aimed at giving the administration time to rebuild the US cattle herd. Agricultural groups have been split: some ranchers back mandatory country-of-origin labeling as a boost to domestic producers and consumer transparency, while groups reliant on imports have opposed the broader tariff-relief push as disadvantaging US producers.

media.caption: Trump signs an executive order on beef country-of-origin labeling amid a push to lower record beef prices

title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump's USPS Mail-In Ballot Rule for Third Time as Voting Begins
detail: US District Judge Indira Talwani (District of Massachusetts) issued a preliminary injunction Friday, September 4, 2026, blocking a new Postal Service rule dictating how states and voters may mail general-election ballots, ruling it likely unlawful and unconstitutional as an intrusion on states' power to regulate their own elections. Talwani found the administration's compressed implementation timeline — coming as mail-in ballots were already going out for the midterms — made 'voter disenfranchisement practically inevitable.' It was the third time a federal court has blocked the Trump administration's effort to restrict mail voting through the Postal Service; the administration asked the Supreme Court over the weekend to allow the rule to take effect while the appeal proceeds.

media.caption: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's Postal Service rule on mail-in ballots for the third time
